items.statement: Prevent molds from growing in drug ingredients and, when feasible and valuable, remove all molds that may contaminate them.
items.quote: It is important to prevent molds from growing in drug ingredients and when feasible and valuable remove all molds that may contaminate such ingredients.

items.statement: When assessing the risk of viral contamination of an animal-derived ingredient, consider both the viral load of the raw material (e.g. tissue, glands, blood) and the viral clearance capability of the ingredient manufacturing process.
items.quote: The probability of an animal virus contaminating an animal-derived ingredient will depend on the viral load of the raw material (e.g., tissue, glands, blood) and the viral clearance capability of the drug ingredient manufacturing process. Both of these factors should be considered when assessing the risk of viral contamination of the ingredient.

items.statement: Protect against prion contamination by obtaining bovine meat and meat byproducts from animals not infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy, and by protecting product against contamination with high-risk tissues, especially brain and spinal cord.
items.quote: Protection from prion contamination includes obtaining bovine meat and meat byproducts from animals not infected with bovine spongiform encephalopathy and protecting against contamination of product with high-risk tissues, especially brain and spinal cord tissue.

items.statement: When importing bovine material into the United States, be familiar with and comply with all import eligibility requirements and government regulations on food and drugs.
items.quote: Drug manufacturers importing bovine material into the United States should be familiar with and adhere to all import eligibility requirements and government regulations pertaining to food and drugs.
items.condition: when importing bovine material into the United States

items.statement: Base contamination control on strategies that prevent contamination, not on final testing or examination alone; a control strategy relying on testing alone is not compliant.
items.quote: The drug component and finished product CGMP guidances and regulations emphasize prevention of problems and avoidance of contamination rather than final testing or examination alone. In other words, control strategies that prevent contamination are central to CGMP, while control strategies based on testing alone do not comply with CGMP regulations.

items.statement: When animal-derived material is used, obtain it from healthy, disease-free animals.
items.quote: When animal-derived material is used, it is important that it be derived from healthy, disease-free animals.

items.statement: Understand the pathogenic risks associated with different animal species and with different organs, glands or tissues within a species.
items.quote: Ingredient manufacturers should understand the pathogenic risks associated with different animal species and with different organs, glands, or tissues within species.

items.statement: Recognise that even healthy source animals can be reservoirs of pathogenic agents and that improper handling can spread contamination.
items.quote: Drug ingredient manufacturers should be aware that even healthy animals can be reservoirs for pathogenic agents and improper handling can spread contamination.

items.statement: Consider auditing the livestock processing establishments that supply raw materials, and ensure they comply with all Federal and State government regulations.
items.quote: Ingredient manufacturers should consider auditing the LPEs supplying raw materials to them and ensure their compliance with all Federal and State government regulations.
